object_description: two elongated structures placed one after another along the square, with a two-thirds sunken gymnasium
design_condition: the volumes are aligned along the square around a shared schoolyard at square level, with the gymnasium sunk into the ground so that its roof becomes an elevated playing field

positive: Clear urban situation, well suited to school operation
Splitting the programme into several buildings creates positive outdoor spaces at different levels
Separate structures allow differentiated building depths adapted to the uses
The gymnasium keeps a recognisable facade and enlivens the schoolyard in the evening
Public uses can be entered from both sides and used independently of the school
Very careful and convincing incorporation of the historic manor house
15 m ceiling span gives a high degree of flexibility
Classified as cost-effective, with average operating and maintenance costs
Considered the most balanced proposal in urban and operational terms
negative: Second-stage primary school volume is not convincing in position or design
Relationship between the kindergarten units and their outdoor spaces is not sufficiently formulated
Copying the school wing floor plan for the second stage is unconvincing in this location
Room programme for changing, equipment and material rooms needs revision; a 70 m2 equipment room is missing
Force transmission through the thermal insulation leads to numerous thermal bridges
Narrow axial dimensions on the south side require a large number of solar shading elements
